text:
Marta CS: customer reported a sudden drop in embeddings throughput this morning — vectors/sec down ~6x compared to yesterday. they say tokens/sec looks flat. they’re hitting our /v1/embeddings endpoint.

Aisha SRE: ack, can you paste the request pattern and any errors they see?

Marta CS: pasted from customer logs:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
{
  \"model\": \"embed-large-1024\",\n  \"input\": ["short text 1", "short text 2", ...]\n}
```
They get successful 200s, but vectors/sec measured by their client drops from ~1200 -> ~180. They also saw sporadic "dimension mismatch" warnings in app logs when they concat batches.

Tom Runtime: weird that tokens/sec is flat but vectors/sec drops. that suggests maybe batching changed and batch-to-vector throughput relation broken. any chance our batching config for the embeddings runtime was changed? I’ll check deploy history.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-10T04:12Z by tom-runtime -> inference/embeddings: runtime-2.3.1 -> 2.4.0 (flags: continuous_batching=false, batch_window_ms=50)

Tom Runtime: aha — continuous_batching disabled in 2.4.0. that can drastically reduce vectors/sec for short inputs because we’re emitting more small batches. tokens/sec can look OK if tokenization docs are different.

Leo ML: also, dimension mismatch messages could be from an opportunistic client-side concat after partial result ordering changes. we changed output ordering for micro-batches in 2.4.0 to reduce tail latency. if customers expect strict per-request ordering and they concatenate by index, short-circuit can cause shape mismatches.

Aisha SRE: action plan: 1) reproduce against canary cluster with continuous_batching=false and true, 2) capture GPU metrics (util, SM%, memory bw), queue depth, and per-request batch sizes, 3) get sample curl from customer to repro dim-mismatch. I can run load tests.

Marta CS: customer willing to share sample payload and will try temporary config override if we provide one. they’re on Dedicated.

Tom Runtime: repro steps from my side: curl with 1000 concurrent short inputs (avg length 8 tokens). run one test with continuous_batching=false then true. commands: 
```
# quick loadgen using vegalab client
vega load --host https://dedicated.customer.redwood/v1/embeddings \\
  --api-key $KEY --model embed-large-1024 --qps 400 --batch-size 64 --inputs-file small_inputs.json
```
Collect /metrics/gpu, /metrics/queue_depth, /metrics/batch_size_dist.

Aisha SRE: I ran a short run on canary: with continuous_batching=false we see average batch size ~3, vectors/sec ~210, GPU util ~28%, queue depth higher (~220). with continuous_batching=true batch size ~18, vectors/sec ~1250, GPU util ~82%, queue depth lower. So the regression is consistent.

Leo ML: that fits. continuous batching lets us amortize kernel overhead for small inputs — vectors/sec scales with batch size more than tokens/sec for embeddings. dimension mismatch: can we see trace where a response for micro-batch reorders? share application logs.

Marta CS: pasted customer excerpt: 
```
[WARN] embed_worker.py: unexpected vector dim 768 != 1024 for request id abc-123
stack: concat_vectors -> bulk_store -> assert dim
```
They say this happens ~1/1000 requests.

Tom Runtime: likely two different model variants getting mixed (quantized vs full) in fallback path when continuous batching is off and single-request fast path triggers. maybe the routing logic falls back to compact-quant variant which returns 768 dims. I'll look at routing logs.

infra-bot: routing.log excerpt 2026-03-12T11:05Z:
```
route: embeddings/region-us -> node-7 (model: embed-large-1024-quant)
route: embeddings/region-us -> node-3 (model: embed-large-1024)
```

Tom Runtime: yep, two variants registered with same model name. when de-dup logic for continuous_batching=false picks a fallback fast path, it used node-7 which is quant variant. that explains dim mismatch. fix: make routing choose consistent model family or ensure quantized variants return same dimension (not typical).

Aisha SRE: short-term mitigations: 1) re-enable continuous_batching globally for embeddings until we roll a safer change; 2) add an assert in routing to prevent mixing incompatible model variants in the same serving pool; 3) provide customer a temporary route pin to node-3 only.

Tom Runtime: I can rollback the flag on canary and then schedule a hotfix to rollout. Repro run after enabling continuous batching on canary shows vectors/sec recovered to ~1200 and dimension mismatch errors dropped to 0 in 10k requests.

Marta CS: customer confirmed after we pinned them to node-3 vectors/sec recovered to expected. they saw one more dim-mismatch right after pin then none. they’re happy with temporary fix but want permanent fix.

Leo ML: long-term: normalize model variants so quantized outputs pad or convert to same dimensionality when advertised under same model id, and add CI check for model family mismatches. also change default rollout to not flip continuous_batching off without a safety gate.

Aisha SRE: follow-ups assigned: Tom to rollback flag (ETA 30m), Tom+Infra to add routing assert (PR), Leo to spec model-variant compatibility checks, Marta to update customer.

Tom Runtime: starting rollback now. command: `kubectl patch configmap embeddings-runtime -p '{\"data\":{\"continuous_batching\":\"true\"}}'`

deploy-bot: patch accepted, rollout started -> embeddings-runtime/replica-set scaled 3 -> 5

Aisha SRE: monitoring: after rollback we should watch these dashboards: embeddings/batch_size, embeddings/vectors_per_sec, nodes/gpu_util, routing/mismatch_rate. I’ll schedule a 2h watch.

Marta CS: noted, customer wants a postmortem and permanence timeline. they ask: any risk to latency for their tail requests with batching re-enabled?

Tom Runtime: enabling continuous batching slightly increases p99 for tiny requests (~10-20ms) but keeps throughput and reduces cost. we’ll document tradeoffs and offer per-customer route pins if strict ordering or micro-latency needed.

Leo ML: adding test cases to our loadgen harness to include short-sequence, high-concurrency embedding workloads so we catch regressions earlier.

Marta CS: thanks team — I’ll send customer summary and repro notes. will update thread when PRs are in. :thumbsup:

Aisha SRE: PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4521 (routing assert)

Tom Runtime: rollback complete on canary and prod ramp underway. monitoring looks good so far — vectors/sec back within 5% of baseline, gpu util up. closing loop after 2h watch.

Marta CS: customer confirmed steady state at t+90m. we can write postmortem.

infra-bot: incident-tag: throughput-regression-embed-2026-03-12

Marta CS: assigning postmortem owners: Tom, Aisha, Leo.

Tom Runtime: creating postmortem doc and will include repro commands, metrics, and remediation timeline.

Marta CS: thanks all.
